# Sealed Recipes

> A marketplace on NEAR where an expert's workflow (a "recipe") runs on a user's data inside sealed hardware. The user never sees the method, the creator never sees the data, and one on-chain settlement pays everyone who contributed. Paid per run. Built for the NEAR Hackathon, November 2026.

Source, tests and full documentation: https://github.com/ztoori/sealed-recipes (MIT). Start with AGENTS.md there if you are an AI agent.

## Why it exists

- New apps, features and agents arrive faster than anyone can read their rules. Most people skip the reading and learn the hard way.
- A few people do the reading and turn it into a workflow across many tools and documents: a recipe. It is their edge, and it is hard to sell: paywalls, copyright and licences all leak, and one copy is enough.
- Here the recipe is sealed to an attested runner. It is sold one run at a time and never handed over.

## Who it is for

- Users (people or AI agents): pick a recipe, get a signed quote, pay per run. A failed run is refunded by the contract.
- Creators: compose recipes from parts without code, seal them, earn on every run.
- Builders: write parts (code, agents, model calls, data sources) to the open spec SRS-1, earn a fee each time a part is used.
- Runners: run recipes inside confidential hardware (Intel TDX), earn a fee on every run.

## What is live

- Site: https://sealedrecipes.xyz (NEAR testnet, test token tUSDC, no login). Film: https://sealedrecipes.xyz/#/demo
- Contract: market.sealedrecipes.testnet. Payment token: tusdc.sealedrecipes.testnet. Runner: tee.sealedrecipes.testnet (Intel TDX, dstack on Phala Cloud).
- Live recipes: CHECK (contract check before you sign), SAFE3 (wallet scam scan), AUDIT3 (account security audit). They read public NEAR mainnet data, read-only.
- Not live: mainnet, wallet connect, NEAR Intents payments (Intents has no testnet; the local demo exercises that path against a mock), more than one runner, a reproducible runner build.

## HTTP API of the live site (JSON)

- GET /api/mode: network, contract, payment token, runner
- GET /api/listings: recipes with price, risk, parts, form fields and the on-chain track record
- GET /api/catalog: the parts (SRS-1 manifests: ports, capabilities, fees, disclosure, limits)
- GET /runner/attestation?nonce=HEX: the runner's TDX quote and keys; GET /api/tee/collateral: Intel-signed collateral to verify it
- POST /api/quotes: { recipe_id, sealed_job, ... } returns a quote signed by the runner, from a sealed dry run
- POST /api/runs/prepare, then pay with ft_transfer_call from your own key, then POST /api/runs/:id/paid, then GET /api/runs/:id/events
- POST /api/faucet: { account_id } funds a guest key with test tokens (rate limited)
- GET /healthz

A complete client is scripts/agent-buyer.ts in the repository: `npm run agent -- --live` verifies the runner, collects signed quotes, picks one by a policy, pays, and checks the runner's signature and the settlement.

## Pages

- /#/recipes: the listings. /#/quote/CHECK: get a quote and run. /#/wallet: guest account.
- /#/compose/recipe and /#/compose/part: the practice composer (simulated services).
- /#/docs/spec: SRS-1. /#/docs/trust: every check, and what each party can see. /#/docs/runner: how the runner works.
